tldr: Stock sync will be built without line-based mapping; plain SKU and quantity is enough, and kits can work if the message marks what is a kit.
Once stock sync lands, chasing CSV and Edifact over SFTP can be done without Snap-specific reporting, which supports the multi-WMS north star.
Multiple Shopify connectors on one store look like a non-issue because the Poland and UK setups are separate businesses with separate stock pools in Snap. This will be validated in QA.
A few transaction history items remain before the announcement, and a dedicated observability dashboard is wanted.
Snap load testing is waiting on other testing to finish. Snap has a host with prod-equivalent hardware to simulate against.
decisions: Skip line-based mapping for stock sync; it is overkill and stock is just SKU and amount.
Kits are acceptable as long as the data denotes what is a kit and what is not.
Treat multiple Shopify connectors against one store as a non-issue because the businesses are separate, but validate it in QA.

actions.text: Look into observability and metrics for stock sync, including a distinct dashboard, outside the sprint.
Finish the remaining transaction history work before announcing stock sync.
Run Snap load testing against Snap's prod-spec host once the current testing wraps up, and share the results in Confluence.
Validate in QA that multiple Shopify connectors on the same store do not cause duplicate stock mutations.
Share the orient skill packs for meeting transcription so Speaker 1 can bake them into their daybook.

questions: Does the stock sync message need a specific format so it can be passed into Edifact and sent for the Tilburg customer?
